title: Hardship Review Guidelines: Restart Percent on Deficiency Balance Accounts
content:
**Guideline.** On an account held under Deficiency Balance Accounts, the restart percent (the percentage of the balance at which a restart down payment is figured) is lowered for documented hardship on the account's own arrangement offers. When an arrangement offer of the account whose offer date falls fewer than 12 whole months before today carries a Social Security award letter or a physician's medical disability statement as its hardship document, the restart percent is lowered by 3.0 points; when no such offer carries either of those but one carries a state unemployment benefit determination, it is lowered by 1.5 points; otherwise hardship lowers the restart percent by no points. Whole months are counted as the difference in calendar months between the two dates, less one when the later date's day of the month is below the earlier date's.

## The guideline as a table

| Hardship documents on the account's offers dated fewer than 12 whole months before today | Restart percent lowered by |
|---|---|
| At least one Social Security award letter or medical disability statement (with or without an unemployment determination) | 3.0 points |
| No award letter or disability statement, at least one unemployment determination | 1.5 points |
| None of the three | No points |

Every arrangement offer of the account counts, whatever its kind (plan or settlement) and whatever its status; the hardship document is read from the offer record. The points are not added up across several offers: an account with two qualifying offers is lowered once, by the figure of the row it falls in.

## Look-back boundary (hypothetical dates)

Today is the 10th of a month.

| Offer date | Whole months before today | Inside the look-back? |
|---|---|---|
| The 11th of the same month a year earlier | 11 | Yes |
| The 10th of the same month a year earlier | 12 | No |
| The 9th of the same month a year earlier | 12 | No |

## Basis Q&A

**An offer within the look-back carries an unemployment determination and an older offer carries an award letter.** Only offers inside the look-back count, so the restart percent is lowered by 1.5 points.

**The only qualifying offer was declined by the borrower.** It still counts; the guideline reads the hardship document on any offer of the account in the look-back.
